sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Restless History, continuing our epic World Cup-themed sweep through 32 countries of the world that have qualified for the Football World Cup in Qatar.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《不安的历史》，我们将继续以世界杯为主题，巡礼 32 个获得卡塔尔世界杯参赛资格的国家。

sentences.en: And today, Dominic, we come to, I would guess, the country that probably has the least history.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，今天我们来到了一个我猜可能是历史上最没存在感的国家。

sentences.en: The least history that perhaps people in this country have heard of any country.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是这个国家的人民自己都没怎么听说过历史的国家。

sentences.en: And that is Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 那就是哥斯达黎加。

sentences.en: Come on, Tom, you're not a favourite Costa Rican history?
sentences.zh: 得了吧，汤姆，你难道不是哥斯达黎加历史的忠实粉丝吗？

sentences.en: This is unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 这简直难以置信。

sentences.en: So Costa Rica is, I mean, Costa Rica is famous for its wildlife, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以哥斯达黎加，我的意思是，哥斯达黎加是以野生动物闻名的，对吧？

sentences.en: It is indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's famous for its red-eyed tree frogs.
sentences.zh: 它以红眼树蛙而闻名。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's famous for its tremendous program of reforestation.
sentences.zh: 它以其卓越的植树造林计划而闻名。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a great ecotourism destination, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，它是一个很棒的生态旅游目的地。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And of course, it's famous for its dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 当然，它还以恐龙而闻名。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know much about Costa Rican dinosaurs, to be sure.
sentences.zh: 好吧，说实话，我对哥斯达黎加的恐龙了解不多。

sentences.en: Well, you do.
sentences.zh: 不，你了解的。

sentences.en: You do.
sentences.zh: 你了解的。

sentences.en: It's best-known tourist attraction, Jurassic Park, on the Isla Nublar.
sentences.zh: 它最著名的旅游景点就是努布拉岛上的《侏罗纪公园》。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: But the history, I know nothing about it.
sentences.zh: 但关于它的历史，我一无所知。

sentences.en: Well, Tom, I'll tell you what.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，我来告诉你。

sentences.en: To make it accessible for you.
sentences.zh: 为了让你更容易理解。

sentences.en: Now, I know we said from the very beginning of this World Cup series that it absolutely wasn't going to be about football.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们在本届世界杯系列节目一开始就说过，这绝对不是关于足球的。

sentences.en: But we will start with a tiny bit of football, just a tiny bit, I promise.
sentences.zh: 但我们还是会从一点点足球开始，就一点点，我保证。

sentences.en: So, the 2014 World Cup, which was held in Brazil, Group D.
sentences.zh: 那么，2014 年在巴西举办的世界杯，D 组。

sentences.en: England were drawn in Group D.
sentences.zh: 英格兰队被抽到了 D 组。

sentences.en: And they were drawn along with Italy, Uruguay, and Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 和他们分在一起的还有意大利、乌拉圭和哥斯达黎加。

sentences.en: So, a tough group.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个死亡之组。

sentences.en: Three former winners.
sentences.zh: 有三支前冠军球队。

sentences.en: England, Italy, and Uruguay.
sentences.zh: 英格兰、意大利和乌拉圭。

sentences.en: And lots of people in England said, well, this will be really hard, but at least we'll get three points against the Costa Ricans.
sentences.zh: 当时很多英格兰人都说，好吧，这会非常艰难，但至少我们能从哥斯达黎加人身上拿到三分。

sentences.en: Tom, do you know who finished top of that group?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你知道是谁以小组第一出线的吗？

sentences.en: Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 哥斯达黎加。

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是他们。

sentences.en: And do you know who finished bottom?
sentences.zh: 那你知道谁垫底吗？

sentences.en: England.
sentences.zh: 英格兰。

sentences.en: England.
sentences.zh: 英格兰。

sentences.en: Absolutely right now.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The thing is, we should have known better than to underestimate the Costa Ricans, because that was actually their fourth World Cup, and they have qualified for six.
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们本该知道不能低估哥斯达黎加人，因为那实际上是他们第四次参加世界杯，而且他们总共已经六次入围了。

sentences.en: And that World Cup in 2014, they went on to reach the quarterfinals, and they came within a penalty shootout of reaching the semifinals.
sentences.zh: 在那届 2014 年世界杯上，他们一路打进了四分之一决赛，距离半决赛仅一步之遥，最后输在了点球大战。

sentences.en: It's an extraordinary accomplishment for such a small Central American country.
sentences.zh: 对于这样一个中美洲小国来说，这是一项非凡的成就。

sentences.en: And actually, when you step back from that and you look at it, Costa Rica, as I said, is in Central America.
sentences.zh: 实际上，当你退一步审视时，正如我所说，哥斯达黎加位于中美洲。

sentences.en: And their neighbours, so Nicaragua, Honduras, El Salvador, Guatemala, Panama, none of them have had anything like the same kind of sporting success that Costa Rica have had.
sentences.zh: 而它的邻国，比如尼加拉瓜、洪都拉斯、萨尔瓦多、危地马拉、巴拿马，它们都没有取得过像哥斯达黎加那样出色的体育成就。

sentences.en: And generally, as you probably know, Tom, in sport, as in so much else, it's actually money and stability.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你可能也知道，在体育领域，就像在其他许多方面一样，关键其实在于金钱和稳定。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Costa Rica is a very stable country, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 哥斯达黎加是一个非常稳定的国家，不是吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So when you look at that list of countries, Nicaragua, Honduras, El Salvador, Guatemala, many of those countries are some of the most violent countries in the world,
sentences.zh: 所以当你看看那份国家名单，尼加拉瓜、洪都拉斯、萨尔瓦多、危地马拉，其中许多国家是世界上最暴力的国家之一，

sentences.en: higher homicide rates, higher imprisonment rates than anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 它们的凶杀率和监禁率比其他任何地方都高。

sentences.en: They're politically, historically very unstable, and they're also extremely poor.
sentences.zh: 它们在政治和历史上都非常不稳定，而且极其贫穷。

sentences.en: But if you look at any ranking in Latin America, Costa Rica is not merely the safest country in Central America.
sentences.zh: 但如果你查看拉丁美洲的任何排名，哥斯达黎加不仅是中美洲最安全的国家。

sentences.en: So as you said, an extremely popular ecotourism destination where you can be pretty confident that you won't get into any trouble.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它是一个极其受欢迎的生态旅游目的地，你可以非常确信在那里不会遇到任何麻烦。

sentences.en: But it's one of the most affluent countries in Latin America.
sentences.zh: 而且它是拉丁美洲最富裕的国家之一。

sentences.en: So it's comparable only really with Uruguay, Chile and Argentina.
sentences.zh: 所以它真正能与之相比的只有乌拉圭、智利和阿根廷。

sentences.en: So the country's right in the south.
sentences.zh: 那个国家就在南边。

sentences.en: Now, when you look at it superficially, there's no obvious reason why that should be the case.
sentences.zh: 现在，当你从表面上看时，没有明显的理由说明为什么会这样。

sentences.en: Because in Costa Rica, they have the same Spanish language.
sentences.zh: 因为在哥斯达黎加，他们说着同样的西班牙语。

sentences.en: They have the same custoMs.
sentences.zh: 他们有着同样的习俗。

sentences.en: They have the same kind of ethnicity as people do in Nicaragua and Honduras and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们和尼加拉瓜、洪都拉斯等地的人有着同样的种族背景。

sentences.en: So what is the explanation?
sentences.zh: 那么解释是什么呢？

sentences.en: Why is Costa Rica such an outlier?
sentences.zh: 为什么哥斯达黎加是一个特例？

sentences.en: And to answer that, Tom, do you know where we need to go back to?
sentences.zh: 为了回答这个问题，汤姆，你知道我们需要回到什么时候吗？

sentences.en: No, I literally know nothing about the history of Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 不，我对哥斯达黎加的历史一无所知。

sentences.en: I cannot put into words how little I know about the history of Costa Rica, because I know nothing, nothing, literally nothing.
sentences.zh: 我无法用言语来形容我对哥斯达黎加的历史有多么无知，因为我什么都不知道，真的，什么都不知道。

sentences.en: I'll be frank with you.
sentences.zh: 我跟你说实话。

sentences.en: You're going to be educated.
sentences.zh: 你将会受到教育。

sentences.en: You don't even need to educate yourself because I will do it.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不需要自己去学习，因为我会教你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We are going back to the Costa Rican Civil War of the 1940s.
sentences.zh: 我们要回到 20 世纪 40 年代的哥斯达黎加内战。

sentences.en: Very exciting, Tom.
sentences.zh: 非常刺激，汤姆。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Who knew that they'd had a civil war?
sentences.zh: 谁知道他们竟然打过内战？

sentences.en: I suppose Costa Ricans do, but not many people.
sentences.zh: 我想哥斯达黎加人知道，但没多少人知道。

sentences.en: People were distracted by the stuff that was going on in the 1940s, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想当时人们都被 40 年代发生的其他事情分散了注意力。

sentences.en: And their eyes were not on Costa Rica, where the main action was happening.
sentences.zh: 他们的目光并没有投向哥斯达黎加，而那里才是当时主要行动发生的地方。

sentences.en: So, okay, let's pull the camera right back.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们把镜头拉远一点。

sentences.en: If you're in Costa Rica in the 1940s, where are you?
sentences.zh: 如果你身处 40 年代的哥斯达黎加，你在哪里？

sentences.en: So the bottom end of Central America, you've got Nicaragua to the north, you've got Panama to the south.
sentences.zh: 在中美洲的最南端，北边是尼加拉瓜，南边是巴拿马。

sentences.en: And historically, this has been the backwater of backwaters.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，这里一直是穷乡僻壤中的穷乡僻壤。

sentences.en: So before the Spanish came to the Americas, there were obviously people in Costa Rica, pre-Columbian people,
sentences.zh: 所以，在西班牙人来到美洲之前，哥斯达黎加显然有人居住，也就是前哥伦布时期的人民，

sentences.en: but there weren't great empires and cities as there were in what are now Mexico and Peru.
sentences.zh: 但那里并没有像现在的墨西哥和秘鲁那样伟大的帝国和城市。

sentences.en: The Spanish called it the Costa Rica, the kind of the rich coast, basically from hope rather than anything else.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人称它为“哥斯达黎加”，也就是“富饶的海岸”，这基本上是出于希望而非其他任何原因。

sentences.en: They hoped there would be gold there.
sentences.zh: 他们希望那里有黄金。

sentences.en: So like Greenland.
sentences.zh: 就像格陵兰岛一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: He's calling it Greenland.
sentences.zh: 他管那叫格陵兰岛。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Marketing scam.
sentences.zh: 营销骗局。

sentences.en: They hope there's gold.
sentences.zh: 他们希望那里有黄金。

sentences.en: And there's a tiny bit of gold, but there's not very much.
sentences.zh: 确实有一点点黄金，但不多。

sentences.en: And it takes them ages to conquer it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们花了很长时间才征服它。

sentences.en: They basically don't conquer it for about 50 years.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上花了大约 50 年才征服它。

sentences.en: Almost all the indigenous people are wiped out through disease.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有的原住民都因疾病而灭绝了。

sentences.en: And after that, basically, I mean, to cut a very long story short, nothing ever really happens in Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，基本上，长话短说，哥斯达黎加从来没发生过什么大事。

sentences.en: It's very underpopulated.
sentences.zh: 它人口非常稀少。

sentences.en: There's no native labor.
sentences.zh: 没有本地劳动力。

sentences.en: So there's no point establishing a big kind of hacienda, the big kind of estates that people establish in much of Latin America.
sentences.zh: 所以建立那种拉丁美洲大部分地区常见的大庄园毫无意义。

sentences.en: It's very poor.
sentences.zh: 它非常贫穷。

sentences.en: It's very sparsely populated.
sentences.zh: 人口非常稀疏。

sentences.en: It's kind of peasants.
sentences.zh: 基本上都是农民。

sentences.en: Even the governor, the Spanish colonial governor,
sentences.zh: 甚至连总督，那位西班牙殖民总督，

sentences.en: has to basically farm his own crops and even kind of look after his own garden because there aren't enough domestic servants and laborers and things to do it for him.
sentences.zh: 都必须亲自耕种庄稼，甚至还要打理自己的花园，因为没有足够的家仆和劳工来为他做这些事。

sentences.en: And as you no doubt know, at the end of the Napoleonic Wars, much of what's new, new Spain breaks away from Madrid.
sentences.zh: 正如你无疑知道的那样，拿破仑战争结束后，大部分“新西班牙”地区脱离了马德里的统治。

sentences.en: And so Costa Rica becomes independent, kind of despite itself.
sentences.zh: 于是哥斯达黎加在某种程度上被迫独立了。

sentences.en: And it goes from one entity to another.
sentences.zh: 它从一个实体转变为另一个实体。

sentences.en: It's part of the Mexican Empire.
sentences.zh: 它曾是墨西哥帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: It's part of what's called the Federal Republic of Central America.
sentences.zh: 它曾是所谓“中美洲联邦共和国”的一部分。

sentences.en: At one point, some American adventurers even tried to take it over and fail.
sentences.zh: 甚至一度有美国冒险家试图接管它，但失败了。

sentences.en: But it ends up as this kind of independent republic.
sentences.zh: 但最终它成为了这样一个独立的共和国。

sentences.en: And in the 19th century, the big thing that happens is coffee.
sentences.zh: 在 19 世纪，发生的大事是咖啡。

sentences.en: So in the 1820s, the coffee trade really takes off.
sentences.zh: 19 世纪 20 年代，咖啡贸易真正兴起。

sentences.en: And actually, the biggest customer is Britain.
sentences.zh: 实际上，最大的客户是英国。

sentences.en: So they start an Anglo-Costa Rican bank for coffee growers.
sentences.zh: 所以他们为咖啡种植者创办了一家英属哥斯达黎加银行。

sentences.en: They build a railway from the coffee estates to the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们修建了一条从咖啡庄园到海岸的铁路。

sentences.en: And this presumably is when the deforestation happens.
sentences.zh: 想必这就是森林砍伐发生的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: They're now busy repairing.
sentences.zh: 他们现在正忙着修复。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: But even so, Costa Rica is still very underpopulated.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，哥斯达黎加的人口仍然很少。

sentences.en: No big cities, no big estates.
sentences.zh: 没有大城市，没有大庄园。

sentences.en: There's not much to fight over.
sentences.zh: 没什么可争夺的。

sentences.en: And so although there's a bit of turbulence in its politics,
sentences.zh: 所以尽管其政治上有一点动荡，

sentences.en: they're nothing like as turbulent as in Latin American countries where there's a lot of tension between big mercantile cities and kind of agricultural magnates.
sentences.zh: 但远没有其他拉丁美洲国家那样动荡，那些国家在大商业城市和农业巨头之间存在着巨大的紧张关系。

sentences.en: The other thing about Costa Rica in the 19th century, before we get back to 1940, we often completely forget this in English-speaking world.
sentences.zh: 关于 19 世纪的哥斯达黎加，在我们回到 1940 年之前，还有一件事，我们在英语世界经常完全忘记这一点。

sentences.en: Latin America was often very progressive.
sentences.zh: 拉丁美洲往往是非常进步的。

sentences.en: So they abolished the death penalty in 1871.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在 1871 年就废除了死刑。

sentences.en: They had freedom of religion.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有宗教自由。

sentences.en: They had separation of church and state and the separation of kind of the judiciary and the legislature and the executive.
sentences.zh: 他们实现了政教分离，以及司法、立法和行政权的分离。

sentences.en: So they're quite forward thinking.
sentences.zh: 所以他们非常有前瞻性。

sentences.en: And their politics is not ideological.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的政治不是意识形态导向的。

sentences.en: It's all about patrons and big bosses, which makes it very confusing.
sentences.zh: 一切都是关于赞助人和大老板，这让情况变得非常混乱。

sentences.en: So that's all the sort of context.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是所有的背景。

sentences.en: So the president at the turn of the 1940s is a bloke called Raphael Angel Calderon, and he is a doctor.
sentences.zh: 40 年代初的总统是一个叫拉斐尔·安赫尔·卡尔德隆的家伙，他是一名医生。
zh_words: 拉斐尔·安赫尔·卡尔德隆

sentences.en: He's been educated, interestingly, in Belgium.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他在比利时受过教育。

sentences.en: So almost everybody in this story that we're going to meet has kind of European links somewhere or other.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个故事中我们要遇到的几乎每个人，在某处都有某种欧洲联系。

sentences.en: And he had become president as the sort of the friend of the coffee oligarchs, as they're known.
sentences.zh: 他成为总统时，是所谓的“咖啡寡头”的朋友。

sentences.en: So the people who control the coffee estates.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些控制咖啡庄园的人。

sentences.en: A coffee oligarch.
sentences.zh: 咖啡寡头。

sentences.en: Yeah, you could be a coffee oligarch.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以当个咖啡寡头。

sentences.en: What a thing to be.
sentences.zh: 那可真是个了不起的身份。

sentences.en: There's a lot of money in coffee.
sentences.zh: 咖啡里有很多钱。

sentences.en: But over time, like a lot of Latin American politicians in the same period, he becomes more and more populiSt.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，就像同一时期的许多拉丁美洲政客一样，他变得越来越民粹主义。

sentences.en: And he sort of carries out welfare policies and health care.
sentences.zh: 他开始推行福利政策和医疗保健。

sentences.en: But he doesn't start wearing epilettes or any of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有开始穿那种带肩章的制服之类的东西。

sentences.en: He doesn't.
sentences.zh: 他没有。

sentences.en: He doesn't quite go that far.
sentences.zh: 他还没到那个地步。

sentences.en: Now, in Costa Rica, there's a constitutional provision that you can't run for consecutive terms as president.
sentences.zh: 在哥斯达黎加，宪法规定总统不能连任。

sentences.en: So Mr. Calderon, Senor Calderon, can't run again.
sentences.zh: 所以卡尔德隆先生，也就是卡尔德隆阁下，不能再次参选。

sentences.en: And he gets basically a sort of dog's body of his.
sentences.zh: 于是他找了个类似傀儡的人来接替他。

sentences.en: So this is kind of Putin behavior.
sentences.zh: 这有点像普京的做法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Putin in Medvedev.
sentences.zh: 普京和梅德韦杰夫那样。

sentences.en: Like Medvedev.

sentences.zh: 哥斯达黎加历史上的大人物，汤姆。

sentences.en: So, um, I told you before the break, if you were listening, as I hope you were, that all the people in this story had European connections.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我在休息前告诉过你，如果你当时在听的话，我希望你在听，这个故事里的所有人都有欧洲背景。

sentences.en: And this is Senator Don Pepe.
sentences.zh: 这就是佩佩参议员。

sentences.en: His parents were from Barcelona and he'd been born in Costa Rica in 1906, just after they immigrated to Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 他的父母来自巴塞罗那，他于1906年出生在哥斯达黎加，就在他们移民到哥斯达黎加之后。

sentences.en: And he, his Catalan identity was always very important to him.
sentences.zh: 而且他，他的加泰罗尼亚身份对他来说一直非常重要。

sentences.en: He's very independent minded, is Figueres.
sentences.zh: 菲格雷斯非常有独立思想。

sentences.en: Like the Catalans tend to be.
sentences.zh: 就像加泰罗尼亚人通常那样。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Well, that's why he sort of says, I'm, I'm Catalan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是为什么他会说，我，我是加泰罗尼亚人。

sentences.en: I'm always very Catalan.
sentences.zh: 我一直是非常加泰罗尼亚式的。

sentences.en: I'm very strong-willed.
sentences.zh: 我意志非常坚定。

sentences.en: Um, he's sent to a seminary.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他被送进了神学院。

sentences.en: He doesn't like it at all.
sentences.zh: 他一点也不喜欢那里。

sentences.en: He drops out in the 1920s and he goes off to Boston to study at MIT, Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪20年代退学，去了波士顿，在麻省理工学院学习。

sentences.en: But he's studying hydroelectric science at MIT.
sentences.zh: 但他当时在麻省理工学院学习水力科学。

sentences.en: And he finds it unsurprisingly, I think it's fair to say, very boring.
sentences.zh: 而且他发现这门学科，我想说实话，非常无聊，这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he drops out of that as well.
sentences.zh: 所以他也从那里退学了。

sentences.en: And he puts himself through a curriculum he's devised himself of reading at the Boston Public
sentences.zh: 他为自己制定了一套课程，在波士顿公共图书馆阅读。

sentences.en: Library.
sentences.zh: 图书馆。

sentences.en: And he reads Cervantes.
sentences.zh: 他读塞万提斯。

sentences.en: He reads Kant.
sentences.zh: 他读康德。

sentences.en: He reads Nietzsche.
sentences.zh: 他读尼采。

sentences.en: And he reads HG Wells.
sentences.zh: 他读赫伯特·乔治·威尔斯。

sentences.en: So he's a, he's a clever man.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个，他是个聪明人。

sentences.en: He comes back to Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 他回到了哥斯达黎加。

sentences.en: He becomes a big, um, coffee grower.
sentences.zh: 他成为了一个大，嗯，咖啡种植者。

sentences.en: And you will delight you to hear, Tom, he is a manufacturer of rope, which I know from your reading of Patrick O'Brien.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你听到这个一定会很高兴，他还是个绳索制造商，我从你读帕特里克·奥布莱恩的书里知道这一点。

sentences.en: You're very interested in him.
sentences.zh: 你对他很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I'm against him.
sentences.zh: 我反对他。

sentences.en: So he, he is a, he's a philanthropiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他，他是一个，他是一个慈善家。

sentences.en: He's very kindly kind of Victorian paternalist employer.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常和蔼的、维多利亚时代的家长式雇主。

sentences.en: He builds houses for his workers.
sentences.zh: 他为他的工人们盖房子。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Now maybe he's, maybe I'm not against him then.
sentences.zh: 那也许他，也许我又不反对他了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: You were harsh on Dr. Valverde.
sentences.zh: 你对瓦尔韦德博士太苛刻了。

sentences.en: Yes, I was now dead.
sentences.zh: 是的，我现在死了。

sentences.en: And you cannot afford to be harsh on Don Pepe.
sentences.zh: 而且你不能对佩佩苛刻。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I'm, I'm all for Don Pepe.
sentences.zh: 我，我完全支持佩佩。

sentences.en: He establishes a nice vegetable farm for his workers.
sentences.zh: 他为他的工人们建立了一个很棒的蔬菜农场。

sentences.en: Oh, FIFA Don Pepe.
sentences.zh: 哦，佩佩万岁。

sentences.en: And a dairy with free milk.
sentences.zh: 还有一个提供免费牛奶的奶牛场。

sentences.en: So what's not to like?
sentences.zh: 那还有什么不满意的呢？

sentences.en: He's a great fellow.
sentences.zh: 他是个了不起的人。

sentences.en: Anyway, uh, he's a kindly man.
sentences.zh: 总之，呃，他是个和蔼的人。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say to his, to his sort of workers.
sentences.zh: 我想说，对他，对他那种工人来说是这样的。

sentences.en: But in the early 1940s, he had become increasingly alarmed by the authoritarian direction of the
sentences.zh: 但在20世纪40年代初，他开始对卡尔德隆政府的威权主义倾向感到越来越担忧。

sentences.en: Calderon administration.
sentences.zh: 卡尔德隆政府。

sentences.en: And he had in fact been exiled for two years in Mexico because he'd said this, this sort of, um, authoritarian president is going to end up as a communist and you should watch out.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他曾在墨西哥流亡了两年，因为他说，这个，这个，嗯，威权总统最终会变成共产主义者，你们应该小心。

sentences.en: He comes home and in the run-up to that election, he had become a major figure in something called the Caribbean Legion.
sentences.zh: 他回到家，在选举前夕，他成为了一个名为“加勒比军团”组织的重要人物。

sentences.en: And the Caribbean Legion is a kind of pro-democracy group across the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 加勒比军团是一个遍布加勒比地区的亲民主组织。

sentences.en: They're very opposed to the dictator Somoza in Nicaragua and Rafael Trujillo, the horrible dictator in the Dominican Republic.
sentences.zh: 他们非常反对尼加拉瓜的独裁者索摩查和多米尼加共和国可怕的独裁者拉斐尔·特鲁希略。

sentences.en: And one of their members, Tom, who you'll definitely have heard of, and we won't need to provide an invented pen portrait of, is a young man called Fidel Castro.
sentences.zh: 而他们的成员之一，汤姆，你肯定听说过，我们不需要再编造什么肖像画了，是一个叫菲德尔·卡斯特罗的年轻人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: He's a member of the Caribbean Legion.
sentences.zh: 他是加勒比军团的成员。

sentences.en: So they, the Caribbean Legion think, basically, if we can have Costa Rica as a democratic base in Central America, then we can spread democracy to the rest of Central America.
sentences.zh: 所以他们，加勒比军团认为，基本上，如果我们能让哥斯达黎加成为中美洲的民主基地，那么我们就能把民主传播到中美洲的其他地区。

sentences.en: And Figueres, Don Pepe is very keen on this.
sentences.zh: 而菲格雷斯，佩佩对此非常热衷。

sentences.en: And when he hears about the murder of Dr. Valverde, not as you claim an experimenter on frock, but a, but a lovely, a kindly, kindly gentleman.
sentences.zh: 当他听到瓦尔韦德博士被谋杀的消息时，他不是你所说的那个在长袍上做实验的人，而是一个，而是一个可爱、和蔼、和蔼的绅士。

sentences.en: I think it's fair, more accurate to say a man of whom we know absolutely, you and I know absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 我认为更准确的说法是，一个你和我对他一无所知的人。

sentences.en: But maybe, maybe, but Dominic, maybe, maybe we have some, who knows, perhaps some Costa
sentences.zh: 但也许，也许，但是多米尼克，也许，也许我们有一些，谁知道呢，也许有一些哥斯达黎加听众。

sentences.en: Rican listeners.
sentences.zh: 黎加听众。

sentences.en: And if we do, or we have any, anybody who knows anything about Costa Rican history, they could tell us.
sentences.zh: 如果我们有，或者我们有任何了解哥斯达黎加历史的人，他们可以告诉我们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I can assure you, I have scoured what few books there are on Costa Rican history, and I can find nothing about Dr. Valverde.
sentences.zh: 我可以向你保证，我查阅了现有的关于哥斯达黎加历史的少数几本书，我找不到任何关于瓦尔韦德博士的信息。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Anyway, listen, Figueres decides, this is my chance, basically.
sentences.zh: 总之，听着，菲格雷斯决定，这基本上是我的机会。

sentences.en: Figueres is Don Pepe, just to, just to be clear.
sentences.zh: 菲格雷斯就是佩佩，为了，为了清楚起见。

sentences.en: It's Don Pepe, yes.
sentences.zh: 是佩佩，没错。

sentences.en: I'll call him Figueres from that throughout.
sentences.zh: 我从头到尾都叫他菲格雷斯。

sentences.en: Let's put Don Pepe because he sounds too much like a pizza or something.
sentences.zh: 我们还是叫佩佩吧，因为他听起来太像披萨之类的东西了。

sentences.en: He sounds like a brand of sherry, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他听起来像个雪利酒品牌，不是吗？

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: He's actually not a pizza at all.
sentences.zh: 他其实根本不是披萨。

sentences.en: That would be Italian.
sentences.zh: 那是意大利的东西。

sentences.en: He's a, he's a brand of sherry.
sentences.zh: 他是一个，他是一个雪利酒品牌。

sentences.en: He's not, he's, he's Figueres.
sentences.zh: 他不是，他，他是菲格雷斯。

sentences.en: He's a very impressive person.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: Figueres says, right, this is it.
sentences.zh: 菲格雷斯说，好吧，就是现在。

sentences.en: We're going to have to trigger an uprising to, to, to, you know, the election has been stolen and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们必须引发一场起义，因为，因为，因为，你知道，选举被窃取了，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And he's raised this little army.
sentences.zh: 他组建了这支小军队。

sentences.en: And it's a really weird kind of rag bag of anti-communists, of people who represent the coffee interests, but also people on the left who are, you know, they're, they're, they're
sentences.zh: 这是一群非常奇怪的反共人士，代表咖啡利益的人，但也包括左翼人士，你知道，他们，他们，他们是左翼，但他们支持民主，而且他们怀疑卡尔德隆政权的威权主义。

sentences.en: left wing, but they're pro-democracy and they're suspicious of the kind of, um, of the authoritarianism of the Calderon regime.
sentences.zh: 威权主义。

sentences.en: So this little national liberation army, um, it fights its way into the second city within a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 所以这支小小的民族解放军，嗯，在几周内就打进了第二大城市。

sentences.en: So the, the fighting sort of breaks out in March, um, 1948.
sentences.zh: 所以战斗在1948年3月爆发了。

sentences.en: And by the 20th, 12th of April, they're in Carthago, which is the second largest city.
sentences.zh: 到了4月12日，他们已经进入了第二大城市卡塔戈。

sentences.en: They're kind of carrying more before.
sentences.zh: 他们有点势如破竹。

sentences.en: So Carthage.
sentences.zh: 所以是迦太基。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Named off Carthage.
sentences.zh: 以迦太基命名。

sentences.en: And so this is really becoming quite a theme of our.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的成了我们节目的一个主题。

sentences.en: Carthaginian theme.
sentences.zh: 迦太基主题。

sentences.en: Of our World Cup episodes, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我们世界杯剧集的主题，不是吗？

sentences.en: We've had Dido, we've had, uh, Ganibal.
sentences.zh: 我们有狄多，我们有，呃，汉尼拔。

sentences.en: And now.
sentences.zh: 现在又是这个。

sentences.en: So maybe when the World Cup is over, we can repackage this series, Tom, as, uh.
sentences.zh: 所以也许当世界杯结束后，我们可以重新包装这个系列，汤姆，作为，呃。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The world history.
sentences.zh: 世界历史。

sentences.en: Carthage around the world.
sentences.zh: 环球迦太基。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So basically the support for the government is melting away and they're increasingly reliant on the communist, on this communist militias.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上政府的支持率正在流失，他们越来越依赖共产主义者，依赖这些共产主义民兵。

sentences.en: So the capital is San Jose and the communists are kind of hold up in the capital.
sentences.zh: 所以首都是圣何塞，共产主义者被困在首都里。

sentences.en: And the question is, are they going to hold out while Figueres' little army are approaching
sentences.zh: 问题是，当菲格雷斯的小军队逼近时，他们会坚持到底，还是会接受失败？

sentences.en: or are they going to accept defeat?
sentences.zh: 还是会接受失败？

sentences.en: And it's at this point that the United States is really crucial because of course, this is the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 就在这一点上，美国变得至关重要，因为当然，这是冷战时期。

sentences.en: The Americans are very, very anti-communiSt.
sentences.zh: 美国人非常、非常反共。

sentences.en: And the Americans basically make it plain to the government.
sentences.zh: 美国人基本上向政府表明了立场。

sentences.en: They say, if the communists end up properly taking over, we will send in troops from Panama.
sentences.zh: 他们说，如果共产主义者最终真的接管了政权，我们将从巴拿马派遣军队进入。

sentences.en: So they mobilise.
sentences.zh: 所以他们动员起来了。

sentences.en: They have troops on alert in the canal zone in Panama, ready to step in.
sentences.zh: 他们在巴拿马运河区有处于警戒状态的军队，准备随时介入。

sentences.en: And Picardo, the weedy historian who's still president.
sentences.zh: 还有皮卡多，那位依然担任总统的平庸历史学家。

sentences.en: Oh, he's still there, is he?
sentences.zh: 哦，他还在任上，是吗？

sentences.en: He's still hanging around.
sentences.zh: 他还在那儿混着呢。

sentences.en: He's a bit of a figurehead.
sentences.zh: 他多少算是个挂名首脑。

sentences.en: He sends a message to Calderon and to the communists.
sentences.zh: 他给卡尔德隆和共产党人发了条消息。

sentences.en: And he says, listen, it will be an absolute catastrophe if we have street fighting in the capital.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，如果我们在首都发生街头巷战，那将是一场彻头彻尾的灾难。

sentences.en: Because as a historian, he would know that, wouldn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为作为一名历史学家，他应该知道这一点，不是吗？

sentences.en: That would be a lesson of history that he would draw.
sentences.zh: 那是他能从中汲取的历史教训。

sentences.en: And if he hadn't been a historian, yes, he could have said street fighting would be brilliant.
sentences.zh: 如果他不是历史学家，他当然可以说街头巷战会很精彩。

sentences.en: So this is a victory in some ways for history.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这是历史的胜利。

sentences.en: It's a vindication of history.
sentences.zh: 这是对历史的辩护。

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: So, and he says, basically, the United States will step in and this will be a disaster.
sentences.zh: 所以，他基本上是说，美国会介入，这将是一场灾难。

sentences.en: We can't have this.
sentences.zh: 我们不能让这种情况发生。

sentences.en: So the Picardo, the communists and Calderon, they all agree they will give up.
sentences.zh: 于是皮卡多、共产党人和卡尔德隆都同意放弃。

sentences.en: Calderon goes off to Nicaragua with Picardo, the historian.
sentences.zh: 卡尔德隆和历史学家皮卡多一起去了尼加拉瓜。

sentences.en: So the doctor and the historian are gone.
sentences.zh: 所以医生和历史学家都走了。

sentences.en: The communists just sort of melt away after a bit of fighting.
sentences.zh: 共产党人在经历了一点战斗后就散去了。

sentences.en: On the 24th of April.
sentences.zh: 在4月24日那天。

sentences.en: So, you know, what is it?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: What are we?
sentences.zh: 我们算什么？

sentences.en: Less than two months after the whole business began.
sentences.zh: 距离这一切开始还不到两个月。

sentences.en: Figueres's forces enter San Jose and they take over the government.
sentences.zh: 菲格雷斯的部队进入圣何塞，接管了政府。

sentences.en: So not big death toll.
sentences.zh: 所以伤亡人数并不多。

sentences.en: About 2,000 people.
The war lasted 44 days.
sentences.zh: 战争持续了44天。

sentences.en: Well, wait for it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，等着瞧吧。

sentences.en: Wait for it.
sentences.zh: 等着瞧。

sentences.en: So just to tell you what happened to all the characters.
sentences.zh: 现在告诉你们所有这些角色的结局。

sentences.en: Picardo, the historian, he stayed in Nicaragua forever.
sentences.zh: 历史学家皮卡多永远留在了尼加拉瓜。

sentences.en: He never came back.
sentences.zh: 他再也没回来。

sentences.en: That was the end of him.
sentences.zh: 那就是他的结局。

sentences.en: Calderon, the doctor.
sentences.zh: 医生卡尔德隆。

sentences.en: He goes, he's an exile in Mexico where he bizarrely, he just goes back to being a doctor again.
sentences.zh: 他流亡到了墨西哥，奇怪的是，他又回去当医生了。

sentences.en: Then he comes back to Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 后来他回到了哥斯达黎加。

sentences.en: He runs for president unsuccessfully and ends up as an ambassador to Mexico from Costa Rica, which is quite a sort of, yeah, that's quite a benevolent outcome.
sentences.zh: 他竞选总统失败，最终担任了哥斯达黎加驻墨西哥大使，这算是一个相当仁慈的结局。

sentences.en: Now that is a clue about what happens to Costa Rica.
sentences.zh: 这正是哥斯达黎加后来发生什么的线索。

sentences.en: Because actually everything that we've talked about till now is sort of standard Latin American stuff, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为实际上我们刚才谈论的一切都是拉美的标准戏码，不是吗？

sentences.en: Coups and people called Don Pepe and yeah, all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 政变，还有叫唐·佩佩的人，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But what actually happened, it's what happens that is the difference.
sentences.zh: 但真正发生的事情，才是与众不同的地方。

sentences.en: What happens now?
sentences.zh: 现在发生了什么？

sentences.en: Because Figueres, he takes power for 18 months and he's basically says, I will take power and then I'll give it up.
sentences.zh: 因为菲格雷斯掌权了18个月，他基本上说，我会掌权，然后我会交出权力。

sentences.en: I have no ambition to be a dictator.
sentences.zh: 我没有当独裁者的野心。

sentences.en: This is the guy we talked about as the Catalan who read Cervantes and was a sort of kindly rope employer.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们提到的那个读过塞万提斯的加泰罗尼亚人，一个和蔼的绳索雇主。

sentences.en: And in his 18 months, he gives women the vote.
sentences.zh: 在他执政的18个月里，他赋予了女性投票权。

sentences.en: He abolishes the sort of reading requirements, you know, the literacy requirement for voting.
sentences.zh: 他废除了投票的阅读要求，也就是识字要求。

sentences.en: He confirms the existing welfare legislation.
sentences.zh: 他确认了现有的福利立法。

sentences.en: He nationalizes the banks.
sentences.zh: 他将银行国有化。

sentences.en: He writes a new constitution, expands public education.
sentences.zh: 他制定了新宪法，扩大了公共教育。
